item.text: {"text":"Original SASRec right-aligns histories in a fixed-length array, left-padding with item ID 0 and truncating oldest interactions. Learned absolute positional embeddings index array slots 0…L−1, including padding slots before masking; they are not renumbered from the first real item. Padding states are zeroed before attention and after blocks; attention masks padding keys and uses a lower-triangular causal mask including the diagonal. Training aligns each input item with its immediate successor: `[0,a,b,c] → [0,b,c,d]`; loss ignores zero targets. Inference scores the final slot. These details follow the original [sampler](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py), [model](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py), and [attention implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/modules.py).\n\nPerturbation studies distinguish altered training sequences from fixed-target evaluation: [Woolridge et al.](https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-2955/paper8.pdf) shuffle training histories while preserving held-out validation/test items. For diagnostic controls, inferred from the implementation: shuffle only nonpadding history slots, preserving length, padding, targets, and candidates; optionally hold the latest item fixed to separate earlier-order effects from changing the final query item. Deletion followed by compaction and left-padding changes content, available context, and some surviving items’ absolute positions. Compare it with deletion at identical locations while retaining surviving positions and explicitly masking holes, plus equal-count random deletions. For a position-only control, keep content/order and masks fixed while varying explicit position IDs. With per-position training diagnostics, perturb each target’s preceding prefix separately and retain its original target; globally shuffling inputs against unchanged shifted labels can expose a target within its own causal context. Rebuilding shifted labels instead changes the prediction task. Freeze weights, disable dropout, and repeat perturbations across seeds."}
